⇒ Time for A = 12 months, B = 12 months, C = 12 − 4 = 8 months

⇒ Profit share ratio A : B : C = (3x × 12) : (8x × 12) : (6x × 8)

⇒ A : B : C = 36 : 96 : 48

⇒ Dividing by 12, Profit Ratio = 3 : 8 : 4

⇒ If C profit = 4 parts = ₹24,000

⇒ 1 part = 24,000 ÷ 4 = ₹6,000

⇒ Total Profit = (3 + 8 + 4) parts = 15 parts

⇒ Total Profit = 15 × 6,000 = ₹90,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹90,000.

Additional Information

Basic Partnership Rule

Profit Share Ratio = (Capital1 × Time1) : (Capital2 × Time2). The profit is always distributed based on the product of investment and duration.

Active vs Sleeping Partner

An active partner manages the business and may receive a fixed percentage or salary from the profit before the remaining profit is divided in the investment ratio.

Total Profit Formula

Total Profit = (Sum of all ratio parts) × (Value of one ratio part). Here, Value of one part = Individual Share ÷ Individual Ratio Part.

questions.question: A and B invest in a business in the ratio 4 ∶ 5. After 10 months B leaves the business after withdrawing his investment. In the first year the business made a profit of Rs 49,000. What is B's share (in Rs) of this profit?
questions.questionHtml: A and B invest in a business in the ratio 4 ∶ 5. After 10 months B leaves the business after withdrawing his investment. In the first year the business made a profit of Rs 49,000. What is B's share (in Rs) of this profit?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit Ratio = (CapitalA × TimeA) : (CapitalB × TimeB)

Profit Ratio A : B = (4 × 12 months) : (5 × 10 months) = 48 : 50 = 24 : 25

Total units = 24 + 25 = 49 units → ₹49,000

B's share = 25 units = (49,000 ÷ 49) × 25 = ₹25,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹25000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of investments (A : B) = 4 : 5

Time period for A = 12 months (Full year)

Time period for B = 10 months

Total Profit = ₹49,000

Formula Used:

Profit Share = Investment × Time Duration

Calculations:

⇒ Profit share ratio (A : B) = (4 × 12) : (5 × 10)

⇒ Profit share ratio (A : B) = 48 : 50

⇒ Simplifying the ratio = 24 : 25

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 24 + 25 = 49 units

⇒ 49 units = ₹49,000

⇒ 1 unit = 49,000 ÷ 49 = ₹1,000

⇒ B's share = 25 units = 25 × 1,000

⇒ B's share = ₹25,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹25000.

Additional Information

Basic Partnership Rule

Profit is always distributed in the ratio of the product of capital and the time for which the capital is invested (Profit = C × T).

Ratio of Capital and Time

If profits (P1, P2) and time periods (T1, T2) are known, the ratio of capitals is C1 : C2 = (P1/T1) : (P2/T2).

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and may receive an additional salary or percentage of profit before the remaining profit is divided in the investment ratio.

questions.question: Working together A and B can do a job in 40 days, B and C in 36 days and all three together in 24 days. In how many days can B alone do the job?
questions.questionHtml: Working together A and B can do a job in 40 days, B and C in 36 days and all three together in 24 days. In how many days can B alone do the job?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total work (LCM of 40, 36, and 24) = 360 units.

Efficiency of (A+B) = 9, (B+C) = 10, and (A+B+C) = 15.

Efficiency of B = Eff(A+B) + Eff(B+C) − Eff(A+B+C) = 9 + 10 − 15 = 4 units/day.

Time taken by B alone = 360 ÷ 4 = 90 days.

∴ The correct answer is 90 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by (A + B) = 40 days

Time taken by (B + C) = 36 days

Time taken by (A + B + C) = 24 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = LCM of the time taken by individuals/groups; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
(A + B) 40 360 9
(B + C) 36 10
(A + B + C) 24 15

⇒ Total work = LCM(40, 36, 24) = 360 units

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = 360 ÷ 40 = 9 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of (B + C) = 360 ÷ 36 = 10 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 360 ÷ 24 = 15 units/day

⇒ To find B's efficiency: (EffA+B + EffB+C) − EffA+B+C

⇒ Efficiency of B = (9 + 10) − 15 = 19 − 15 = 4 units/day

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 360 ÷ 4 = 90 days

∴ The correct answer is 90 days.

Additional Information

Individual Efficiency Calculation

If efficiency of (A+B+C) and (A+B) is known, then C's efficiency = Eff(A+B+C) − Eff(A+B). Similarly, A's efficiency = Eff(A+B+C) − Eff(B+C).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by individuals. If they work for the same duration, the wage ratio is equal to the efficiency ratio.

Combined Time Formula

If A can do a work in x days and B in y days, then together they can do it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

questions.question: A, B and C can do a job working alone in 50, 75 and 20 days respectively. They all work together for 4 days, then C quits. How many days will A and B take to finish the rest of the job?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can do a job working alone in 50, 75 and 20 days respectively. They all work together for 4 days, then C quits. How many days will A and B take to finish the rest of the job?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total work = LCM(50, 75, 20) = 300 units.

Efficiencies: A = 6, B = 4, C = 15. Total (A+B+C) = 25 units/day.

Work done in 4 days = 25 × 4 = 100 units.

Remaining work = 300 − 100 = 200 units.

Days taken by A and B to finish the rest = 200 ÷ (6 + 4) = 20 days.

∴ The correct answer is 20 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A = 50 days

Time taken by B = 75 days

Time taken by C = 20 days

Total work = LCM of (50, 75, 20) = 300 units.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 50 300 units 300 ÷ 50 = 6
B 75 300 ÷ 75 = 4
C 20 300 ÷ 20 = 15

Calculations:

⇒ Total efficiency of (A + B + C) = 6 + 4 + 15 = 25 units/day.

⇒ Work done by A, B, and C in 4 days = 25 × 4 = 100 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 300 − 100 = 200 units.

⇒ Efficiency of A and B = 6 + 4 = 10 units/day.

⇒ Days taken by A and B to complete remaining work = 200 ÷ 10 = 20 days.

∴ The correct answer is 20 days.

Additional Information

Relationship between Time and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Total Work Calculation

Total work is generally assumed to be the LCM of the individual number of days for easier calculation of efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

The same logic applies to pipes and cisterns where filling pipes have positive efficiency and outlet pipes have negative efficiency.

questions.question: A can do 50% of the job in 16 days, B can do 1/4th of the job in 24 days. In how many days can they do 3/4 th of the job working together?
questions.questionHtml: A can do 50% of the job in 16 days, B can do 1/4th of the job in 24 days. In how many days can they do 3/4<sup>th</sup> of the job working together?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Full time taken by A = 16 × 2 = 32 days.

Full time taken by B = 24 × 4 = 96 days.

LCM of (32, 96) = 96 units (Total Work).

Combined efficiency of (A + B) = (96 ÷ 32) + (96 ÷ 96) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day.

Time for 3/4th work = (3/4 × 96) ÷ 4 = 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days.

∴ The correct answer is 18 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Work done by A in 16 days = 50% = 1/2

Work done by B in 24 days = 1/4

Formula:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Time to complete full work for A = 16 ÷ (1/2) = 32 days.

Time to complete full work for B = 24 ÷ (1/4) = 96 days.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 32 96 3
B 96 1

Calculations:

⇒ Total Efficiency (A + B) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Target Work = 3/4th of Total Work = 3/4 × 96 = 72 units

⇒ Time required = Target Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time required = 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days

∴ The correct answer is 18 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x:y, then the ratio of their efficiencies is y:x.

Combined Work Formula

If A can do a work in X days and B in Y days, together they can do it in (X × Y) ÷ (X + Y) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each person, which is the same as the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.

questions.question: A and B can together complete a task in 18 hours. After 6 hours A leaves. B takes 36 hours to finish rest of the task. How many hours would A have taken to do the task, if he worked alone?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can together complete a task in 18 hours. After 6 hours A leaves. B takes 36 hours to finish rest of the task. How many hours would A have taken to do the task, if he worked alone?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Remaining work time for (A + B) = 18 − 6 = 12 hours.

B takes 36 hours to finish this remaining 12-hour work of (A + B).

Efficiency Ratio (A + B) : B = Time ratio inverse = 36 : 12 = 3 : 1.

Efficiency of A = Efficiency (A + B) − Efficiency of B = 3 − 1 = 2 units.

Time taken by A alone = (Efficiency of A + B × Total Time) ÷ Efficiency of A = (3 × 18) ÷ 2 = 27 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 27 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by (A + B) together = 18 hours

Work done by (A + B) in 6 hours = 6 ÷ 18 = 1/3

Remaining work = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3

⇒ B takes 36 hours for 2/3 of the task.

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 36 × (3/2) = 54 hours.

Formula Used:

Total Work = LCM of individual times; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

Person Time (hrs) Total Work Efficiency
A + B 18 54 units 54 ÷ 18 = 3
B 54 54 ÷ 54 = 1

Calculations:

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 3 − 1 = 2 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 54 ÷ 2 = 27 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 27 hours.

Additional Information

Inverse Relation of Time and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x : y, then the ratio of their efficiency is y : x.

Combined Work Formula

If person A takes x hours and person B takes y hours to complete a work individually, then together they will take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual, which matches the efficiency ratio if they work for the same duration.

questions.question: 1 packet of biscuits costs Rs. 16, but a pack of 4 of the same packet of biscuits costs Rs. 56. What is the effective discount (in %) on the pack?
questions.questionHtml: 1 packet of biscuits costs Rs. 16, but a pack of 4 of the same packet of biscuits costs Rs. 56. What is the effective discount (in %) on the pack?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Marked Price of 4 individual packets = 4 × 16 = Rs. 64.

Selling Price of the combined pack = Rs. 56.

Effective Discount Amount = 64 − 56 = Rs. 8.

Effective Discount % = (8 ÷ 64) × 100 = 12.5%.

∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of 1 packet of biscuits = Rs. 16

Cost of a combined pack of 4 packets = Rs. 56

Formula Used:

Discount % = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price

Calculations:

⇒ Marked Price (MP) for 4 separate packets = 4 × 16 = Rs. 64

⇒ Selling Price (SP) for the pack of 4 = Rs. 56

⇒ Discount = MP − SP

⇒ Discount = 64 − 56 = Rs. 8

⇒ Discount % = (8 ÷ 64) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 8) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 12.5%

∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.

Additional Information

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP) or Retail Price of an article. Selling Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are applied on an item, the effective single discount percentage is calculated as: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Buy X Get Y Free

The effective discount percentage in promotional offers is determined by the total items received. Effective Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.

questions.question: The cost price of an article is Rs. x. It is marked up by 200%. It is sold at Rs. 540 after giving 25% discount. What is the value of x (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: The cost price of an article is Rs. x. It is marked up by 200%. It is sold at Rs. 540 after giving 25% discount. What is the value of x (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of CP : MP = 100 : (100 + 200) = 1 : 3

Ratio of MP : SP = 100 : (100 − 25) = 4 : 3

Combined Ratio CP : MP : SP = (1 × 4) : (3 × 4) : (3 × 3) = 4 : 12 : 9

9 units = Rs. 540 ⇒ 1 unit = 60

Value of x (CP) = 4 units = 4 × 60 = 240

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 240.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. x

Markup % = 200%

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 540

Discount % = 25%

Formula Used:

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (100 + Markup %)/100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount %)/100

Calculations:

⇒ 540 = MP × (100 − 25)/100

⇒ 540 = MP × 75/100

⇒ 540 = MP × 3/4

⇒ MP = (540 × 4) ÷ 3 = 180 × 4 = 720

⇒ MP = CP × (100 + 200)/100

⇒ 720 = x × 300/100

⇒ 720 = 3x

⇒ x = 720 ÷ 3

⇒ x = 240

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 240.

Additional Information

Relationship Between CP, MP, and Discount

The direct relation is given by: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%).

Net Profit Percentage

Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount%)/100. In this case, Profit% = 200 − 25 − (200 × 25)/100 = 175 − 50 = 125%.

Successive Discounts

If multiple discounts are applied, the final SP = MP × (1 − d1/100) × (1 − d2/100) ... where d1 and d2 are discount rates.

questions.question: A Rs. 750 tin of cheese is offered at 8% discount and a Rs. 1,250 tin of butter at 20% discount. If we buy 5 tins of cheese and 3 tins of butter, what is the effective discount we get (in %)?
questions.questionHtml: A Rs. 750 tin of cheese is offered at 8% discount and a Rs. 1,250 tin of butter at 20% discount. If we buy 5 tins of cheese and 3 tins of butter, what is the effective discount we get (in %)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total MP of Cheese = 5 × ₹750 = ₹3750

Total MP of Butter = 3 × ₹1250 = ₹3750

Since the total Marked Prices for both items are equal (₹3750 each), the weight ratio is 1 : 1.

Effective Discount % = Average of individual discounts = (8% + 20%) ÷ 2 = 14%.

∴ The correct answer is 14%.

Alternate Method

Given:

MP of cheese tin = ₹750, Discount = 8%

MP of butter tin = ₹1250, Discount = 20%

Quantity: Cheese = 5 tins, Butter = 3 tins

Formula Used:

Effective Discount % = (Total Discount ÷ Total Marked Price) × 100

⇒ Total MP = (5 × 750) + (3 × 1250)

⇒ Total MP = 3750 + 3750 = ₹7500

⇒ Total Discount = (8% of 3750) + (20% of 3750)

⇒ Total Discount = (8 ÷ 100 × 3750) + (20 ÷ 100 × 3750)

⇒ Total Discount = 300 + 750 = ₹1050

⇒ Effective Discount % = (1050 ÷ 7500) × 100

⇒ Effective Discount % = 105 ÷ 7.5 = 14%

∴ The correct answer is 14%.

Additional Information

Weighted Average Discount

When multiple items with different marked prices and discount rates are combined, the net discount rate is the weighted average: (MP1d1 + MP2d2) ÷ (MP1 + MP2).

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts d1% and d2% on a single item, the single equivalent discount is (d1 + d2 − d1d2 ÷ 100)%.

Discount vs Profit

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), while Profit or Loss is generally calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

questions.question: The selling price of an article is Rs. 816. The discount on it is 15%. What would be the selling price of the article (in Rs.) if the discount on it is 25%?
questions.questionHtml: The selling price of an article is Rs. 816. The discount on it is 15%. What would be the selling price of the article (in Rs.) if the discount on it is 25%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of the selling prices is proportional to (100 − Discount%).

Ratio SP1 : SP2 = (100 − 15) : (100 − 25) = 85 : 75 = 17 : 15.

Given 17 units = ₹816 → 1 unit = 816 ÷ 17 = ₹48.

New selling price (15 units) = 15 × 48 = ₹720.

∴ The correct answer is ₹720.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Selling Price (SP1) = ₹816

Initial Discount (D1) = 15%

New Discount (D2) = 25%

Formula Used:

Marked Price (MP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − D%)

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 816 × 100 ÷ (100 − 15)

⇒ MP = (816 × 100) ÷ 85

⇒ MP = 9.6 × 100 = ₹960

⇒ New Selling Price (SP2) = MP × (100 − 25) ÷ 100

⇒ SP2 = 960 × 75 ÷ 100

⇒ SP2 = 960 × 3 ÷ 4

⇒ SP2 = 240 × 3 = ₹720

∴ The correct answer is ₹720.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP)

The price written on the tag of an article is the Marked Price or List Price. Discount is always calculated on MP.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d1% and d2% are given, the net discount = (d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2 ÷ 100))%.

Relation between CP and MP

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is given by CP ÷ MP = (100 − D%) ÷ (100 + P%), where D is discount and P is profit.

questions.question: The entry ticket at a fun park was increased in the ratio 7 : 9, due to which footfalls fell in the ratio 13 : 11. What is the new daily collection (in Rs.), if the daily collection before the price hike was Rs. 2,27,500?
questions.questionHtml: The entry ticket at a fun park was increased in the ratio 7 : 9, due to which footfalls fell in the ratio 13 : 11. What is the new daily collection (in Rs.), if the daily collection before the price hike was Rs. 2,27,500?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Prices = 7 : 9

Ratio of Footfalls = 13 : 11

Ratio of Daily Collection = (7 × 13) : (9 × 11) = 91 : 99

Given: 91 units = ₹2,27,500 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹2,500

New Collection = 99 units = 99 × 2,500 = ₹2,47,500

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,47,500.

Alternate Method

Given:

Old Price : New Price = 7 : 9

Old Footfalls : New Footfalls = 13 : 11

Initial Daily Collection = ₹2,27,500

Formula Used:

Daily Collection = Entry Ticket Price × Number of Footfalls

Calculations:

⇒ Let Old Price = 7x and New Price = 9x

⇒ Let Old Footfalls = 13y and New Footfalls = 11y

⇒ Old Daily Collection = 7x × 13y = 91xy

⇒ Given: 91xy = 2,27,500

⇒ xy = 2,27,500 ÷ 91

⇒ xy = 2,500

⇒ New Daily Collection = 9x × 11y = 99xy

⇒ New Daily Collection = 99 × 2,500

⇒ New Daily Collection = 2,47,500

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,47,500.

Additional Information

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together (antecedent with antecedent and consequent with consequent), the resulting ratio is called the compound ratio. Here, (7:9) compounded with (13:11) gives (91:99).

Percentage Change in Product

If a value is a product of two variables, the net percentage change can be calculated using the formula: a + b + (a × b)/100, where a and b are the percentage changes in the two variables.

Price and Quantity Relationship

Revenue or Expenditure is always directly proportional to both Price and Quantity. If Price increases by ratio a:b and Quantity changes by c:d, the Revenue changes by (a×c):(b×d).

questions.question: If 6A = 4B = 9C; What is A : B : C?
questions.questionHtml: If 6A = 4B = 9C; What is A : B : C?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify the coefficients of A, B, and C which are 6, 4, and 9.

Find the LCM of 6, 4, and 9 which is 36.

Divide the LCM by each coefficient to get the ratio: A = 36 ÷ 6, B = 36 ÷ 4, C = 36 ÷ 9.

A : B : C = 6 : 9 : 4.

∴ The correct answer is 6 : 9 : 4.

Alternate Method

Given: 6A = 4B = 9C

Formula: If xA = yB = zC, then A : B : C = (1/x) : (1/y) : (1/z)

⇒ Let 6A = 4B = 9C = k

⇒ A = k/6, B = k/4, C = k/9

⇒ A : B : C = (k/6) : (k/4) : (k/9)

⇒ Multiplying the entire ratio by the LCM of (6, 4, 9), which is 36:

⇒ A : B : C = (k/6 × 36) : (k/4 × 36) : (k/9 × 36)

⇒ A : B : C = 6k : 9k : 4k

⇒ A : B : C = 6 : 9 : 4

∴ The correct answer is 6 : 9 : 4.

Additional Information

Inverse Ratios

When variables are related by products like aX = bY, the ratio X:Y is inversely proportional to their coefficients, i.e., X:Y = b:a.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios (a : b) and (c : d) is (ac : bd).

Ratio in Fractional Form

To convert fractional ratios (1/a : 1/b : 1/c) to whole numbers, multiply each term by the LCM of the denominators a, b, and c.

questions.question: If 50 less had applied and 25 less selected, the ratio of selected to unselected would have been 9 : 4. How many candidates had applied, if the ratio of selected to unselected was 2 : 1?
questions.questionHtml: If 50 less had applied and 25 less selected, the ratio of selected to unselected would have been 9 : 4. How many candidates had applied, if the ratio of selected to unselected was 2 : 1?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial ratio Applied : Selected = 3 : 2; Final ratio = (9+4) : 9 = 13 : 9

Using cross-multiplication for Applied and Selected changes (−50 and −25):

1 unit = |(13 × 25) − (9 × 50)| ÷ |(3 × 9) − (2 × 13)|

1 unit = |325 − 450| ÷ |27 − 26| = 125

Initial Applied = 3 units = 3 × 125 = 375

∴ The correct answer is 375 candidates.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Selected : Unselected = 2 : 1

Change: Applied − 50, Selected − 25

New Selected : Unselected = 9 : 4

Formula Used:

Total Applied = Selected + Unselected

⇒ Let the initial selected and unselected candidates be 2x and x respectively.

⇒ Total candidates applied initially = 2x + x = 3x.

⇒ New total applied = 3x − 50.

⇒ New selected candidates = 2x − 25.

⇒ New unselected = (New total) − (New selected) = (3x − 50) − (2x − 25) = x − 25.

⇒ New Selected : Unselected = 9 : 4

⇒ (2x − 25) / (x − 25) = 9 / 4

⇒ 4 × (2x − 25) = 9 × (x − 25)

⇒ 8x − 100 = 9x − 225

⇒ 9x − 8x = 225 − 100

⇒ x = 125

⇒ Initial candidates applied = 3x = 3 × 125 = 375.

∴ The correct answer is 375 candidates.

Additional Information

Ratio and Total Value

If a total is divided into two parts in the ratio a : b, the total can be represented as k(a + b) where k is a common multiplier.

Cross Multiplication Rule

For two ratios a:b and c:d with changes x and y, the initial value of 1 unit is given by |(c × y) − (d × x)| ÷ |(a × d) − (b × c)|.

Components of a Population

Total Candidates = Selected + Unselected. Any change in the total population must account for changes in both constituent parts.

questions.question: What is the fourth proportional to 189, 273 and 153?
questions.questionHtml: What is the fourth proportional to 189, 273 and 153?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Fourth Proportional = (Term 2 × Term 3) ÷ Term 1

Required Value = (273 × 153) ÷ 189

Simplified = (13 × 21 × 153) ÷ (9 × 21)

Required Value = 13 × (153 ÷ 9) = 13 × 17

Calculation = 221

∴ The correct answer is 221.

Alternate Method

Given: First term (a) = 189, Second term (b) = 273, Third term (c) = 153

Formula: If a, b, c, d are in proportion, then a ÷ b = c ÷ d ⇒ d = (b × c) ÷ a

⇒ Let the fourth proportional be x.

⇒ 189 : 273 :: 153 : x

⇒ 189 × x = 273 × 153

⇒ x = (273 × 153) ÷ 189

⇒ x = (21 × 13 × 9 × 17) ÷ (21 × 9)

⇒ x = 13 × 17

⇒ x = 221

∴ The correct answer is 221.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(a × b).

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional x is calculated as a : b = b : x, which gives x = b2 ÷ a.

Basic Proportion Rule

In any proportion a : b = c : d, the product of the means (b × c) is always equal to the product of the extremes (a × d).

questions.question: Rs. 11,550 has to be divided between X, Y & Z such that X gets 4/5 of what Y gets and Y gets 2/3 of what Z gets. How much more does Z get over X (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: Rs. 11,550 has to be divided between X, Y & Z such that X gets 4/5 of what Y gets and Y gets 2/3 of what Z gets. How much more does Z get over X (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Combine ratios X : Y = 4 : 5 and Y : Z = 2 : 3 → X : Y : Z = (4×2) : (5×2) : (5×3) = 8 : 10 : 15.

Total Ratio Units = 8 + 10 + 15 = 33 units.

Given 33 units = ₹11,550 → 1 unit = 11,550 ÷ 33 = ₹350.

Difference (Z − X) = 15 − 8 = 7 units.

Value of difference = 7 × 350 = ₹2450.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2450.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total amount = ₹11,550

X = 4/5 of Y

Y = 2/3 of Z

Calculations:

⇒ X/Y = 4/5 and Y/Z = 2/3

⇒ To equalize Y, multiply first ratio by 2 and second by 5:

⇒ X : Y = 8 : 10

⇒ Y : Z = 10 : 15

⇒ Combined Ratio X : Y : Z = 8 : 10 : 15

⇒ Total Share = 8 + 10 + 15 = 33 units

⇒ 33 units = ₹11,550

⇒ 1 unit = 11,550 ÷ 33 = ₹350

⇒ Difference between Z and X = 15 units − 8 units = 7 units

⇒ Value of difference = 7 × 350 = ₹2450

∴ The correct answer is ₹2450.

Additional Information

Ratio Merging Rule

If A:B = m:n and B:C = p:q, then A:B:C = (m×p) : (n×p) : (n×q).

Division of Amount

To find a specific share from a total S in ratio a:b:c, share of A = [a / (a+b+c)] × S.

Proportional Difference

The difference between shares is directly proportional to the difference between their respective ratio parts.

questions.question: Before a battle the ratio of tanks to planes in an army was 5 : 3. During the war 1000 tanks were destroyed and 800 planes were destroyed. The ratio of tanks to planes became 2 : 1. What is the number of tanks after the war?
questions.questionHtml: Before a battle the ratio of tanks to planes in an army was 5 : 3. During the war 1000 tanks were destroyed and 800 planes were destroyed. The ratio of tanks to planes became 2 : 1. What is the number of tanks after the war?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply the cross-multiplication method for ratio change:

Initial Ratio = 5 : 3 | Final Ratio = 2 : 1 | Change = −1000, −800

1 unit difference = |(5 × 1) − (3 × 2)| = 1 unit

Value difference = |(2 × 800) − (1 × 1000)| = 1600 − 1000 = 600

∴ 1 unit = 600. Initial Tanks = 5 × 600 = 3000

Number of tanks after the war = 3000 − 1000 = 2000

∴ The correct answer is 2000 tanks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial ratio of Tanks : Planes = 5 : 3

Tanks destroyed = 1000 | Planes destroyed = 800

Final ratio of Tanks : Planes = 2 : 1

Formula Used:

New Ratio = (Initial Value − Change) / (Initial Value − Change)

Let the initial number of tanks be 5x and planes be 3x.

⇒ (5x − 1000) / (3x − 800) = 2 / 1

⇒ 1 × (5x − 1000) = 2 × (3x − 800)

⇒ 5x − 1000 = 6x − 1600

⇒ 6x − 5x = 1600 − 1000

⇒ x = 600

⇒ Initial number of tanks = 5x = 5 × 600 = 3000

⇒ Number of tanks after the war = 3000 − 1000 = 2000

∴ The correct answer is 2000 tanks.

Additional Information

Ratio Definition

A ratio is a comparison of two or more quantities of the same kind by division, expressed as a : b.

Cross-Multiplication Method

If initial ratio is a:b, final is c:d and changes are p and q, then x = |dq − cp| / |ad − bc|.

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a2 : b2, often used in area-related problems.

questions.question: The average marks of 50 students in an examination was 65. It was later found that the marks of one student had been wrongly entered as 83 instead of 38. The correct average is:
questions.questionHtml: The average marks of 50 students in an examination was 65. It was later found that the marks of one student had been wrongly entered as 83 instead of 38. The correct average is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net change in marks = Correct mark − Wrong mark = 38 − 83 = −45

Change in average = Net change ÷ Number of students = −45 ÷ 50 = −0.9

Correct average = Old average + Change in average = 65 − 0.9 = 64.1

∴ The correct answer is 64.1.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number of students = 50

Initial average marks = 65

Wrongly entered mark = 83

Correct mark = 38

Formula Used:

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of observations

Correct Average = (Total Sum − Wrong Value + Correct Value) ÷ Number of observations

Calculations:

⇒ Total marks (old) = 50 × 65 = 3250

⇒ Correct total marks = 3250 − 83 + 38

⇒ Correct total marks = 3250 − 45 = 3205

⇒ Correct average = 3205 ÷ 50

⇒ Correct average = 64.1

∴ The correct answer is 64.1.

Additional Information

Average Concept

The average (arithmetic mean) is the sum of all values divided by the total count. If one value is changed, the new sum = Old Sum + (New Value − Old Value).

Impact on Average

The change in the average is always equal to the total net change divided by the total number of observations. New Average = Old Average ± (Net Change ÷ n).

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A1 and A2 and sizes n1 and n2 are combined, the combined average = (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.question: In a class of 50 students, there are 22 girls who scored an average of 35 marks in the test. What is the average marks of the boys, if the class average is 42 marks?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 50 students, there are 22 girls who scored an average of 35 marks in the test. What is the average marks of the boys, if the class average is 42 marks?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Girls : Boys = 22 : 28 = 11 : 14

Girls' deficit from class average = 35 − 42 = −7

Total deviation for Girls = 11 × (−7) = −77

Total deviation for Boys must be +77 to balance (Net deviation = 0)

Average surplus for Boys = 77 ÷ 14 = 5.5

Boys' average = Class average + surplus = 42 + 5.5 = 47.5

∴ The correct answer is 47.5 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total students = 50

Number of Girls = 22

Average marks of Girls = 35 marks

Class average marks = 42 marks

Formula Used:

Total Sum = Average × Number of entities

Class Sum = (Girls × Girls' Average) + (Boys × Boys' Average)

Calculations:

⇒ Total marks of the entire class = 50 × 42 = 2100

⇒ Total number of boys = 50 − 22 = 28

⇒ Total marks of the girls = 22 × 35 = 770

⇒ Total marks of the boys = Total class marks − Total girls marks

⇒ Total marks of the boys = 2100 − 770 = 1330

⇒ Average marks of the boys = 1330 ÷ 28

⇒ Average marks of the boys = 47.5

∴ The correct answer is 47.5 marks.

Additional Information

Weighted Average Formula

The combined average of two groups is calculated as A = (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2), where n is the quantity and A is the average.

Deviation Principle

In any distribution, the sum of the deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This is useful for finding missing averages quickly.

Alligation Rule

The ratio of quantities is the inverse of the differences between their individual averages and the mean average: (Quantity1 / Quantity2) = (A2 − Mean) / (Mean − A1).

questions.question: The average of 41 consecutive odd numbers is 49. What is the largest number?
questions.questionHtml: The average of 41 consecutive odd numbers is 49. What is the largest number?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a series of n consecutive odd or even numbers, the relationship between the average and the extreme values is direct:

Largest Number = Average + (n − 1)

Smallest Number = Average − (n − 1)

Given n = 41 and Average = 49:

Largest Number = 49 + (41 − 1) = 49 + 40 = 89

∴ The correct answer is 89.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total consecutive odd numbers (n) = 41

Average of these numbers = 49

Formula Used:

For an Arithmetic Progression (AP) with an odd number of terms, the Average is the middle term.

nth term of AP = a + (n − 1)d

Calculations:

⇒ Since n = 41 (odd), the average is the middle term (21st term).

⇒ Middle term = 49

⇒ Common difference (d) for consecutive odd numbers = 2

⇒ The largest number is the 41st term.

⇒ Number of terms after the middle term = (41 − 1) ÷ 2 = 20

⇒ Largest number = Middle term + (20 × d)

⇒ Largest number = 49 + (20 × 2)

⇒ Largest number = 49 + 40 = 89

∴ The correct answer is 89.

Additional Information

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any series in Arithmetic Progression, Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Smallest Number Formula

In a series of n consecutive odd/even numbers, the smallest number = Average − (n − 1). In this case, 49 − 40 = 9.

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first n consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 is always n2.

questions.question: A batsman scores 87 runs in the 21 st match of his career. His average runs per match increases by 2. What was his average before the 21 st match?
questions.questionHtml: A batsman scores 87 runs in the 21<sup>st</sup> match of his career. His average runs per match increases by 2. What was his average before the 21<sup>st</sup> match?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total increase in runs across all matches = Total matches × Average increase

Total increase = 21 × 2 = 42 runs

Average before the 21st match = Score in 21st match − Total increase

Old Average = 87 − 42 = 45

∴ The correct answer is 45.

Alternate Method

Given:

Score in 21st match = 87

Increase in average = 2

Number of matches before = 20

Formula Used:

Total Runs = Average × Number of matches

Calculations:

Let the average before the 21st match be x.

⇒ Total runs in 20 matches = 20 × x

⇒ Total runs in 21 matches = 20x + 87

⇒ New Average = (20x + 87) ÷ 21

According to the question, New Average = x + 2

⇒ (20x + 87) ÷ 21 = x + 2

⇒ 20x + 87 = 21(x + 2)

⇒ 20x + 87 = 21x + 42

⇒ 21x − 20x = 87 − 42

⇒ x = 45

∴ The correct answer is 45.

Additional Information

Average Score Calculation

The batting average is calculated by dividing the total runs scored by the number of times the batsman has played (total matches, provided he remained not out in none). Formula: Average = Total Runs ÷ Total Innings.

Effect of New Value on Average

If a new value is greater than the current average, the average increases. If the new value is smaller, the average decreases. The change in average = (New Value − Old Average) ÷ New Count.

Total Sum Property

Total Sum = Average × Number of Items. This property is used to find missing values when the average and count are known.

questions.question: Oil, equal to 20% of the weight of groundnut, is extracted in a mill. The matter left after extraction is sold as cattle feed at the rate of Rs. 12.5/kg. The groundnuts are bought at Rs. 20/kg. The processing cost is Rs. 5/kg. At what price (Rs. per kg) should the oil be sold to earn 20% profit on total costs (Total cost = Cost of groundnuts and Processing costs)?
questions.questionHtml: Oil, equal to 20% of the weight of groundnut, is extracted in a mill. The matter left after extraction is sold as cattle feed at the rate of Rs. 12.5/kg. The groundnuts are bought at Rs. 20/kg. The processing cost is Rs. 5/kg. At what price (Rs. per kg) should the oil be sold to earn 20% profit on total costs (Total cost = Cost of groundnuts and Processing costs)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total cost per kg of groundnut = Cost + Processing = 20 + 5 = ₹25.

Total revenue needed per kg of groundnut for 20% profit = 25 × 1.2 = ₹30.

Revenue from residue (80% of 1 kg) = 0.8 × 12.5 = ₹10.

Revenue needed from oil (20% of 1 kg) = 30 − 10 = ₹20.

Selling price of oil per kg = 20 ÷ 0.2 = ₹100.

∴ The correct answer is ₹100.

Alternate Method

Given:

Buying price of groundnut = ₹20/kg

Processing cost = ₹5/kg

Extraction rate of oil = 20% by weight

Cattle feed selling price = ₹12.5/kg

Target profit = 20% on total cost

Let the total weight of groundnuts purchased be 100 kg.

⇒ Total Cost = (100 × 20) + (100 × 5) = 2000 + 500 = ₹2500.

⇒ Target Selling Price = Total Cost × (1 + 20/100) = 2500 × 1.2 = ₹3000.

⇒ Weight of oil extracted = 20% of 100 kg = 20 kg.

⇒ Weight of residue (cattle feed) = 100 − 20 = 80 kg.

⇒ Revenue from cattle feed = 80 kg × ₹12.5/kg = ₹1000.

⇒ Revenue required from oil = Total Revenue − Feed Revenue = 3000 − 1000 = ₹2000.

⇒ Selling Price of oil per kg = 2000 ÷ 20 = ₹100/kg.

∴ The correct answer is ₹100.

Additional Information

Total Cost Concept

Total cost includes procurement cost plus all overheads like processing, labor, and transportation. Profit is always calculated on this final sum unless mentioned otherwise.

By-product Revenue

In manufacturing, revenue from by-products (like cattle feed) reduces the revenue burden required from the main product (oil) to reach the target profit.

Weight Balance Rule

The sum of weights of all outputs (Oil + Residue) must equal the total weight of the raw input (Groundnut) in a closed extraction process.

questions.question: If a vendor sells a coconut at Rs. 14.4, he makes 10% loss. If he wants to make 25% profit, then at what price (in Rs.) should he sell?
questions.questionHtml: If a vendor sells a coconut at Rs. 14.4, he makes 10% loss. If he wants to make 25% profit, then at what price (in Rs.) should he sell?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Loss of 10% → Selling Price is 90% of Cost Price.

Profit of 25% → Selling Price must be 125% of Cost Price.

Required Selling Price = (14.4 ÷ 90) × 125

Required Selling Price = 0.16 × 125 = ₹20.

∴ The correct answer is ₹20.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Selling Price (SP1) = ₹14.4

Loss Percentage = 10%

Desired Profit Percentage = 25%

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Loss%)

New Selling Price (SP2) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ CP = (14.4 × 100) ÷ (100 − 10)

⇒ CP = 1440 ÷ 90 = ₹16

⇒ New Selling Price = 16 × (100 + 25) ÷ 100

⇒ New Selling Price = (16 × 125) ÷ 100

⇒ New Selling Price = 2000 ÷ 100 = ₹20

∴ The correct answer is ₹20.

Additional Information

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. All percentages are calculated on the Cost Price unless specified.

Direct Relation for SP

SP = CP × (100 ± Gain or Loss)% . For multiple changes, use SP2 = SP1 × (Required %)/(Initial %).

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount. Discount% is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP).

questions.question: At a village trade fair, a man buys a horse and a camel together for Rs 51,250. He sold the horse at a profit of 25% and the camel at a loss of 20%. If he sold both the animals at the same price, then the cost price of the cheaper animal was Rs ____________.
questions.questionHtml: At a village trade fair, a man buys a horse and a camel together for Rs 51,250. He sold the horse at a profit of 25% and the camel at a loss of 20%. If he sold both the animals at the same price, then the cost price of the cheaper animal was Rs ____________.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Horse Profit = 25% → CP : SP = 4 : 5

Camel Loss = 20% → CP : SP = 5 : 4

Equalize SP (LCM of 5 and 4 is 20): Horse CP = 16, SP = 20; Camel CP = 25, SP = 20

Ratio of CPHorse : CPCamel = 16 : 25 → Total = 41 units

41 units = ₹51,250 → 1 unit = ₹1,250 → Cheaper animal (16 units) = 16 × 1,250 = ₹20,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹20,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total CP = ₹51,250

Horse Profit% = 25%

Camel Loss% = 20%

Selling Price of Horse (SPH) = Selling Price of Camel (SPC)

Formula: SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%)/100

⇒ SPH = CPH × 125/100 = 5/4 CPH

⇒ SPC = CPC × 80/100 = 4/5 CPC

⇒ Since SPH = SPC, 5/4 CPH = 4/5 CPC

⇒ CPH / CPC = (4/5) / (5/4) = 16/25

⇒ Ratio of Cost Prices = 16 : 25

⇒ Total ratio = 16 + 25 = 41 parts

⇒ 41 parts = ₹51,250

⇒ 1 part = 51,250 ÷ 41 = ₹1,250

⇒ CP of Horse (Cheaper) = 16 × 1,250

⇒ CP of Horse = ₹20,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹20,000.

Additional Information

Ratio of Cost Prices when SP is same

If two articles are sold at the same price with profit/loss percentages P1 and P2, the ratio of their Cost Prices is CP1 : CP2 = 100 ± P2 : 100 ± P1.

Successive Profit/Loss

The effective percentage change can be calculated using the formula: a + b + (ab/100), where positive values denote profit and negative values denote loss.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit = SP − CP; Loss = CP − SP. Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise.

questions.question: On a certain item profit is 150%. If the cost price increases by 25%, what will be the new profit margin (in %)?
questions.questionHtml: On a certain item profit is 150%. If the cost price increases by 25%, what will be the new profit margin (in %)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let initial Cost Price (CP) = 100

Profit = 150% ⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 150 = 250

New CP = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125

New Profit = SP − New CP = 250 − 125 = 125

New Profit % = (New Profit ÷ New CP) × 100 = (125 ÷ 125) × 100 = 100%

∴ The correct answer is 100%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Profit = 150% of CP

Increase in CP = 25%

Formula Used:

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Let CP1 = 100

⇒ Profit = 150% of 100 = 150

⇒ SP = CP1 + Profit = 100 + 150 = 250

⇒ New CP (CP2) = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125

⇒ New Profit = SP − CP2

⇒ New Profit = 250 − 125 = 125

⇒ New Profit % = (New Profit ÷ CP2) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = (125 ÷ 125) × 100 = 100%

∴ The correct answer is 100%.

Additional Information

Markup Percentage

Markup % is calculated on the Cost Price: Markup % = [(Marked Price − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Profit Margin on Selling Price

Sometimes profit is expressed as a percentage of Selling Price: Profit Margin = (Profit ÷ SP) × 100. In this question, if asked on SP, it would be (125 ÷ 250) × 100 = 50%.

Effective Discount

For successive discounts of a% and b%, the single effective discount is [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

questions.question: The passing marks of an exam is 40% marks. A student gets 250 marks and yet fails by 38 marks. What is the maximum marks?
questions.questionHtml: The passing marks of an exam is 40% marks. A student gets 250 marks and yet fails by 38 marks. What is the maximum marks?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Passing marks = Student marks + Marks failed by

Passing marks = 250 + 38 = 288

As per the question, 40% = 288

100% (Maximum marks) = (288 ÷ 40) × 100 = 7.2 × 100 = 720

∴ The correct answer is 720 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Passing Percentage = 40%

Marks Obtained = 250

Shortage for Passing = 38 marks

Formula Used:

Passing Marks = Marks Obtained + Fail Marks

Maximum Marks = (Passing Marks ÷ Passing Percentage) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the maximum marks be X.

⇒ Passing marks required = 250 + 38 = 288

⇒ According to the condition, 40% of X = 288

⇒ (40 ÷ 100) × X = 288

⇒ 0.4 × X = 288

⇒ X = 288 ÷ 0.4

⇒ X = 2880 ÷ 4

⇒ X = 720

∴ The correct answer is 720 marks.

Additional Information

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100. Always use the initial/base value as the denominator.

Conversion of Percentage to Fraction

To convert x% to a fraction, divide by 100. For example, 40% = 40/100 = 2/5.

Reverse Percentage Calculation

If a% of a number is N, then the number is (N ÷ a) × 100. This is the base for finding Maximum Marks.

questions.question: Ravi is 12 years younger than Surya. Ravi's age is 40% of the sum of his and Surya's age. What will be Surya's age 9 years hence?
questions.questionHtml: Ravi is 12 years younger than Surya. Ravi's age is 40% of the sum of his and Surya's age. What will be Surya's age 9 years hence?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Ravi's age to Sum of ages = 40 : 100 = 2 : 5

⇒ Ravi : Surya = 2 : (5 − 2) = 2 : 3

Difference in ratio = 3 − 2 = 1 unit → 12 years

Surya's present age = 3 units = 3 × 12 = 36 years

Surya's age 9 years hence = 36 + 9 = 45 years

∴ The correct answer is 45 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Difference between Surya and Ravi's age = 12 years

Ravi's age = 40% of (Ravi + Surya)

Formula Used:

Percentage = (Value ÷ Total) × 100

Let Ravi's age be R and Surya's age be S.

⇒ S − R = 12 --- (i)

⇒ R = 40% of (R + S)

⇒ R = (40 ÷ 100) × (R + S)

⇒ R = 0.4R + 0.4S

⇒ R − 0.4R = 0.4S

⇒ 0.6R = 0.4S

⇒ R/S = 4/6 = 2/3

⇒ Let R = 2x and S = 3x

⇒ From (i): 3x − 2x = 12

⇒ x = 12

⇒ Surya's present age (S) = 3 × 12 = 36 years

⇒ Surya's age 9 years hence = 36 + 9 = 45 years

∴ The correct answer is 45 years.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two persons remains constant throughout their lives, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of ages of A and B is a : b, and the difference is D, then A's age = [a/(b−a)] × D (if b > a).

Future and Past Ages

Age 'n' years hence = Present age + n; Age 'n' years ago = Present age − n.

questions.question: 5% of a = b, then b% of 20 is the same as __________.
questions.questionHtml: 5% of a = b, then b% of 20 is the same as __________.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the property: x% of y = y% of x.

Given: b = 5% of a

Find: b% of 20 → 20% of b

Substitute b: 20% of (5% of a) = 20% of (a/20)

Calculation check: (20/100) × (a/20) = a/100, which matches b% of 20 = (a/20)% of 20 = a/100.

∴ The correct answer is 20% of a/20.

Alternate Method

Given: 5% of a = b

Formula: x% of y = (x × y) ÷ 100

⇒ 5% × a = b

⇒ (5 ÷ 100) × a = b

⇒ b = a ÷ 20

⇒ We need to find: b% of 20

⇒ (b ÷ 100) × 20 = b ÷ 5

⇒ Substitute value of b: (a ÷ 20) ÷ 5 = a ÷ 100

⇒ Checking Option 4: 20% of a/20 = (20 ÷ 100) × (a ÷ 20) = 1/5 × a/20 = a/100

∴ The correct answer is 20% of a/20.

Additional Information

Percentage Interchange Rule

The property x% of y = y% of x is extremely useful in simplifying calculations like 16% of 50 = 50% of 16 = 8.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage to a fraction, divide by 100. Examples: 5% = 1/20, 20% = 1/5, 25% = 1/4, 50% = 1/2.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by x% and then y%, the net change is given by (x + y + xy/100)%.

questions.question: A man's annual income has increased by Rs 5 lakhs but the tax on income that he has to pay has reduced from 12% to 10%. He now pays Rs 10,000 more income tax. What is his increased income (in Rs lakhs)?
questions.questionHtml: A man's annual income has increased by Rs 5 lakhs but the tax on income that he has to pay has reduced from 12% to 10%. He now pays Rs 10,000 more income tax. What is his increased income (in Rs lakhs)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the initial income be x lakhs.

Tax reduction on old income = (12% − 10%) of x = 2% of x.

Tax on the incremented amount = 10% of 5 lakhs = 0.5 lakh (or ₹50,000).

Net tax increase = Tax on increment − Savings on old income = 0.5 − 0.02x = 0.1 lakh (₹10,000).

0.02x = 0.4 ⇒ x = 20 lakhs. Increased income = 20 + 5 = 25 lakhs.

∴ The correct answer is 25 lakhs.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial tax rate = 12%

New tax rate = 10%

Income increase = ₹5,00,000 (5 lakhs)

Tax increase = ₹10,000 (0.1 lakh)

Formula Used:

Income Tax = Income × Tax Rate

Calculations:

⇒ Let the original annual income be x lakhs.

⇒ Increased annual income = (x + 5) lakhs.

⇒ Old Tax = 12% of x = 0.12x.

⇒ New Tax = 10% of (x + 5) = 0.10 × (x + 5).

⇒ According to the question: New Tax − Old Tax = 0.1 lakh.

⇒ 0.10(x + 5) − 0.12x = 0.1

⇒ 0.1x + 0.5 − 0.12x = 0.1

⇒ 0.5 − 0.1 = 0.12x − 0.1x

⇒ 0.4 = 0.02x

⇒ x = 0.4 ÷ 0.02

⇒ x = 20 lakhs.

⇒ Increased income = x + 5 = 20 + 5 = 25 lakhs.

∴ The correct answer is 25 lakhs.

Additional Information

Effective Tax Rate

It is the actual percentage of income paid as tax after all exemptions and changes in tax slabs. Effective Tax = (Total Tax Paid ÷ Total Income) × 100.

Percentage Change in Tax

When both income and tax rate change, the new tax is calculated on the new base. If rate decreases and income increases, the net tax can increase, decrease, or remain constant depending on the magnitudes.

Direct Proportion in Taxation

If the tax rate is constant, the tax paid is directly proportional to the income. However, in progressive taxation, the rate usually increases with higher income slabs.

questions.question: A racing car going at an average speed of 108 km/hr takes 15 minutes to complete a lap on a racing track. By how much should it increase its speed (in km/hr) to complete the lap in 12 minutes?
questions.questionHtml: A racing car going at an average speed of 108 km/hr takes 15 minutes to complete a lap on a racing track. By how much should it increase its speed (in km/hr) to complete the lap in 12 minutes?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Time ratio (Initial : New) = 15 : 12 = 5 : 4

Since distance of the lap is constant, Speed ratio is the inverse of Time ratio.

Speed ratio (Initial : New) = 4 : 5

Original speed (4 units) = 108 km/hr ⇒ 1 unit = 108 ÷ 4 = 27 km/hr

Required speed increase = (5 − 4) = 1 unit = 27 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 27 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial Speed (S1) = 108 km/hr

Initial Time (T1) = 15 min | New Time (T2) = 12 min

Formula Used: Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance (D) = S1 × T1

⇒ D = 108 × (15 ÷ 60) km

⇒ D = 108 ÷ 4 = 27 km

⇒ Required New Speed (S2) = Distance ÷ T2

⇒ S2 = 27 ÷ (12 ÷ 60) = 27 × 5 = 135 km/hr

⇒ Speed Increase = S2 − S1 = 135 − 108 = 27 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 27 km/hr.

Additional Information

Constant Distance Property

When distance is constant, speed (S) is inversely proportional to time (T). Formula: S1 × T1 = S2 × T2.

Unit Conversion Rules

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

If a car covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

questions.question: Train A takes 45 minutes more than train B to travel a distance of 450 km. Due to engine trouble, the speed of train B falls by a quarter and it takes 30 minutes more than Train A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Train A (in km/hr)?
questions.questionHtml: Train A takes 45 minutes more than train B to travel a distance of 450 km. Due to engine trouble, the speed of train B falls by a quarter and it takes 30 minutes more than Train A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Train A (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed of B falls by 1/4 → Speed Ratio = 4 : 3 ∴ Time Ratio = 3 : 4.

Difference in time for B (1 unit) = Gap 1 (45 mins) + Gap 2 (30 mins) = 75 mins.

Original time of B = 3 units = 3 × 75 = 225 mins.

Time taken by A = 225 + 45 = 270 mins = 4.5 hours.

Speed of A = 450 km ÷ 4.5 hours = 100 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 100 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Distance = 450 km

Time of A − Time of B = 45 mins

New Time of B − Time of A = 30 mins

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:

Let the original speed of B be SB and time taken be TB.

Let the time taken by A be TA.

⇒ TA − TB = 45 / 60 hours = 0.75 hours ....(i)

When speed of B falls by 1/4, new speed = 3/4 × SB.

⇒ New time of B (T'B) = 4/3 × TB.

⇒ T'B − TA = 30 / 60 hours = 0.5 hours ....(ii)

Adding equations (i) and (ii):

⇒ (T'B − TA) + (TA − TB) = 0.5 + 0.75

⇒ T'B − TB = 1.25 hours

⇒ (4/3)TB − TB = 1.25

⇒ (1/3)TB = 1.25 ⇒ TB = 3.75 hours

Now, finding TA from equation (i):

⇒ TA = TB + 0.75 = 3.75 + 0.75 = 4.5 hours

Speed of A = Distance ÷ TA

⇒ Speed of A = 450 ÷ 4.5 = 100 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 100 km/hr.

Additional Information

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed becomes x/y of original, time becomes y/x of original.

Average Speed Formula

When a distance is covered at speed S1 and returned at speed S2, Average Speed = (2 × S1 × S2) ÷ (S1 + S2).

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = |S1 − S2|. For opposite directions, relative speed = S1 + S2.

questions.question: Two cars A and B travel from one city to another, at speeds of 72 km/hr and 90 km/hr respectively. If car B takes 1 hour lesser than car A for the journey, then what is the distance (in km) between the two cities?
questions.questionHtml: Two cars A and B travel from one city to another, at speeds of 72 km/hr and 90 km/hr respectively. If car B takes 1 hour lesser than car A for the journey, then what is the distance (in km) between the two cities?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed ratio of Car A to Car B = 72 : 90 = 4 : 5.

Since distance is constant, the time ratio is the inverse of the speed ratio: 5 : 4.

Difference in time units = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

According to the question, 1 unit = 1 hour.

Distance = Speed × Time = 72 km/hr × 5 hours = 360 km.

∴ The correct answer is 360 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of Car A (SA) = 72 km/hr

Speed of Car B (SB) = 90 km/hr

Difference in time taken (Δt) = 1 hour

Formula Used:

Distance = (Product of Speeds ÷ Difference of Speeds) × Time Difference

Calculations:

Let the distance between the two cities be D km.

⇒ Time taken by Car A = D / 72

⇒ Time taken by Car B = D / 90

⇒ According to the question: (D / 72) − (D / 90) = 1

⇒ (5D − 4D) / 360 = 1

⇒ D / 360 = 1

⇒ D = 360 km

∴ The correct answer is 360 km.

Additional Information

Inversely Proportional Relation

When distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T). If speeds are in ratio a:b, time taken will be in ratio b:a.

Average Speed Formula

If an object covers equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: B starts 4 minutes after A from the same point, for a place at a distance of 7 miles from the starting point. A on reaching the destination turns back and walks a mile where he meets B. If A's speed is a mile in 8 minutes then B's speed is a mile in ____ minutes.
questions.questionHtml: B starts 4 minutes after A from the same point, for a place at a distance of 7 miles from the starting point. A on reaching the destination turns back and walks a mile where he meets B. If A's speed is a mile in 8 minutes then B's speed is a mile in ____ minutes.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance covered by A = 7 + 1 = 8 miles.

Time taken by A = 8 miles × 8 min/mile = 64 minutes.

Since B started 4 minutes late, Time taken by B = 64 − 4 = 60 minutes.

Distance covered by B = 7 − 1 = 6 miles.

B's speed (min per mile) = 60 minutes ÷ 6 miles = 10 minutes/mile.

∴ The correct answer is 10 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total distance to destination = 7 miles.

A's speed = 1 mile in 8 minutes (or 1/8 miles per minute).

A meets B 1 mile away from the destination after turning back.

B starts 4 minutes after A.

Calculations:

⇒ Distance covered by A = Destination distance + Distance back

⇒ Distance covered by A = 7 + 1 = 8 miles.

⇒ Time taken by A = Distance × Pace

⇒ Time taken by A = 8 × 8 = 64 minutes.

⇒ Distance covered by B = Destination distance − Distance from destination

⇒ Distance covered by B = 7 − 1 = 6 miles.

⇒ Since B starts 4 minutes after A, Time taken by B = 64 − 4 = 60 minutes.

⇒ B's speed (minutes per mile) = Total Time ÷ Total Distance

⇒ B's speed = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 minutes/mile.

∴ The correct answer is 10 minutes.

Additional Information

Speed, Time, and Distance Relationship

Distance = Speed × Time. When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time. Pace is often expressed as time per unit distance (e.g., minutes per mile).

Relative Speed

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds. When they move in the same direction, it is the difference.

Meeting Point Problems

In problems where one person reaches a point and returns, the sum of distances covered by both equals twice the total distance if they meet on the return leg: Dtotal = DA + DB = 2 × (Distance to destination).

questions.question: If the amount on a certain principal in 3 years at 12% rate of interest compounded annually is Rs. 12,000, what will be the amount (in Rs.) after the 4 th year?
questions.questionHtml: If the amount on a certain principal in 3 years at 12% rate of interest compounded annually is Rs. 12,000, what will be the amount (in Rs.) after the 4<sup>th</sup> year?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In compound interest, the amount at the end of any year acts as the principal for the next year.

Interest for the 4th year = 12% of ₹12,000

Interest = 12 × 120 = ₹1,440

Amount after 4th year = Amount after 3rd year + Interest of 4th year

Amount = 12,000 + 1,440 = 13,440

∴ The correct answer is ₹13440.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 3 years (A3) = ₹12,000

Rate of interest (R) = 12% per annum

Formula Used:

An+1 = An × (1 + R/100)

Calculations:

⇒ Amount after 4th year = Amount after 3rd year × (1 + 12/100)

⇒ Amount after 4th year = 12000 × (112/100)

⇒ Amount after 4th year = 120 × 112

⇒ Amount after 4th year = 13,440

∴ The correct answer is ₹13440.

Additional Information

Standard CI Formula

The amount A on principal P for n years at R% per annum is given by A = P(1 + R/100)n.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on the same principal and rate is CI − SI = P(R/100)2.

Successive Percentage Growth

Compound interest is an application of successive percentage increase. For two years, the effective rate is (a + b + ab/100)%.

questions.question: The amount (in Rs) received at 10% per annum compound interest after 3 yrs is Rs. 119790. What was the principal?
questions.questionHtml: The amount (in Rs) received at 10% per annum compound interest after 3 yrs is Rs. 119790. What was the principal?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rate 10% = 1/10 → For 3 years, the Principal to Amount ratio is 103 : 113.

Principal : Amount = 1000 : 1331 units.

Given, 1331 units = ₹119790 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹90.

Principal = 1000 × 90 = ₹90000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹90000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount (A) = ₹119790

Rate (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

Formula Used:

A = P(1 + R/100)T

Calculations:

⇒ 119790 = P(1 + 10/100)3

⇒ 119790 = P(11/10)3

⇒ 119790 = P × (1331 ÷ 1000)

⇒ P = (119790 × 1000) ÷ 1331

⇒ P = 90 × 1000

⇒ P = 90000

∴ The correct answer is ₹90000.

Additional Information

Effective Interest Rate

For a 10% rate compounded annually for 3 years, the net effective interest rate is 33.1%. The Amount can be directly calculated as P × 133.1/100.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference (D) between CI and SI for 3 years is given by D = P(R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2T) in the standard formula: A = P(1 + R/200)2T.

questions.question: In how many months will Rs. 8,000 yield Rs. 2,648 as compound interest at 20% per annum compounded semi-annually?
questions.questionHtml: In how many months will Rs. 8,000 yield Rs. 2,648 as compound interest at 20% per annum compounded semi-annually?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rate semi-annually = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% per half-year.

Amount = Principal + Interest = 8,000 + 2,648 = ₹10,648.

Ratio A/P = 10648 ÷ 8000 = 1331/1000 = (11/10)3.

Power 3 implies 3 compounding periods of 6 months each.

Total time = 3 × 6 months = 18 months.

∴ The correct answer is 18 months.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹8,000

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹2,648

Rate (R) = 20% p.a. (Compounded semi-annually)

Formula: A = P(1 + r/100)n

⇒ Amount (A) = P + CI = 8,000 + 2,648 = ₹10,648

⇒ Rate for semi-annual compounding (r) = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% per half-year

⇒ 10,648 = 8,000(1 + 10/100)n

⇒ 10,648 ÷ 8,000 = (1.1)n

⇒ 1.331 = (1.1)n

⇒ (1.1)3 = (1.1)n

⇒ n = 3 half-years

⇒ Time in months = 3 × 6 = 18 months

∴ The correct answer is 18 months.

Additional Information

Semi-annual Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded semi-annually, the annual rate is divided by 2 (R' = R/2) and the number of years is multiplied by 2 (T' = 2T) to get the number of periods.

Quarterly Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded quarterly, the rate is divided by 4 (R' = R/4) and the number of years is multiplied by 4 (T' = 4T).

Effective Rate of Interest

For 10% compounded semi-annually, the effective annual rate is (1 + 10/100)2 − 1 = 21%.

questions.question: What is the rate of interest (in %) if simple interest earned on a certain sum for the 3rd year is Rs. 2,000 and compound interest earned in 2 years is Rs. 4,160?
questions.questionHtml: What is the rate of interest (in %) if simple interest earned on a certain sum for the 3rd year is Rs. 2,000 and compound interest earned in 2 years is Rs. 4,160?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simple interest (SI) is constant for every year → SI for 1st year = ₹2,000.

Total SI for 2 years = 2,000 × 2 = ₹4,000.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = 4,160 − 4,000 = ₹160.

The difference (₹160) is the interest on the 1st year SI (₹2,000).

Rate (R) = (160 ÷ 2,000) × 100 = 8%.

∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Simple Interest for the 3rd year = ₹2,000

Compound Interest for 2 years = ₹4,160

Formula Used:

SI for each year = Total SI ÷ Number of years (Since SI is constant)

CI for 2 years = SI1 + SI2 + Interest on SI1

Rate (R) = (Interest on SI1 ÷ SI1) × 100

⇒ Simple Interest is the same for all years.

⇒ SI for 1st year = SI for 2nd year = SI for 3rd year = ₹2,000.

⇒ Total SI for 2 years = ₹2,000 + ₹2,000 = ₹4,000.

⇒ Difference (D) between CI and SI for 2 years = ₹4,160 − ₹4,000 = ₹160.

⇒ This difference ₹160 is the interest earned on the 1st year interest of ₹2,000 at R%.

⇒ 160 = (2,000 × R × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 160 = 20 × R

⇒ R = 160 ÷ 20

⇒ R = 8%.

∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Additional Information

CI − SI Difference for 2 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given by D = P(R/100)2, which is also the interest on the first year's interest.

Relationship between CI and SI for 2 Years

The ratio of CI to SI for 2 years is given by CI/SI = (200 + R) / 200, where R is the rate of interest per annum.

Effective Rate of Interest

For two years at R%, the effective CI rate is (R + R + R2/100)% whereas the effective SI rate is (2R)%.
